flows.summary: A maintainer points flowmap at a repo, lists its entry points, checks the call graph can walk from them, and writes the briefs that independent mapping agents will follow.

steps.name: Maintainer lists every entry point of the repo into inventory.json
steps.notes: Adapter chosen per [[entry]] in flowmap.toml (or auto-detected); cli adapter turns each top-level script with a __main__ guard into a 'CLI <prog> <stem>' endpoint.

steps.name: Maintainer checks that every entry point's handler is a node the call graph can walk from
steps.notes: Subcommand `check` exits 1 when a handler's file is parsed but has no such node. The same endpoint also serves `impact`, `dump` and the bare summary (see triage-a-change).

steps.name: Maintainer writes the brief one independent mapping agent will follow
steps.notes: Fills flowmap/RUN_SPEC.md with the stack guidance, method text and vocabulary (discovery mode when flowmap.toml has no vocabulary).

flows.summary: A maintainer checks each mapping agent's citations, then merges the independent passes by agreement into one map and a list of questions to decide.

steps.name: Maintainer verifies a pass: every cited anchor exists and every entry point is placed
steps.notes: Pure check; exit code 1 on any BAD citation or MISS endpoint.

steps.name: Maintainer reconciles the passes into map.json by agreement and gets the disputed places as QUESTIONS.md
steps.notes: Reads decisions.json (human pins) and the tests dirs from flowmap.toml; evidence ladder single-source < contested < agreed < tested < confirmed.

flows.summary: A reader looks at the agreed map as diagrams, an interactive atlas, or one left-to-right canvas, to see flows, steps and the code they run.

steps.name: Reader generates Mermaid diagrams of the map at system, flow and step zoom
steps.notes: The generator is the UI: it writes Markdown pages containing mermaid blocks.

steps.name: Reader builds the interactive atlas page of flows, steps, code and shared merge points
steps.notes: Template atlas.template.html is filled with the data as JSON. Reads QUESTIONS.md back by regex (split_votes).

steps.name: Reader builds the canvas: screens, flows, files and written data as one left-to-right picture
steps.notes: With --from it re-reads an existing atlas page's embedded `const DATA` instead of building from the repo.

flows.summary: A reviewer asks, before reading a diff, which flows and steps a change lands on, which entry points can reach a given symbol, and paints the change on the map.

steps.name: Reviewer places a base..head change on the map and gets a verdict (contained, spreads, blind)
steps.notes: Prints markdown (or JSON with --json); nothing is written. Builds the call graph and entry-point set at both git revisions.

steps.name: Reviewer asks which entry points and flows can reach a given symbol
steps.notes: Same CLI endpoint as check-call-graph; `impact` needs map.json (endpoint_flows), `check` does not.

steps.name: Reviewer paints a PR's reach onto the atlas with --pr overlays
steps.notes: Same endpoint as build-atlas; the overlay marks steps as new/direct/reach.

steps.name: Reviewer paints a change, and its story's chapters, onto the canvas with --change
steps.notes: Same endpoint as build-canvas; reads changes/<name>.story.json when present.

flows.summary: A PR author turns a change into a chapter-by-chapter page anchored to the flow map, checks its claims, and shares it as a link that needs no hosting.

steps.name: Author renders the change as chapters on the map, with the story's claims checked against the diff
steps.notes: Reads changes/<name>.story.json if present. --facts prints JSON and --check prints unbacked claims, writing nothing.

steps.name: Author gets a viewer link that carries the whole change page in its URL fragment
steps.notes: The --link flag of the same command; refuses when lint finds problems and trims diff text past BUDGET.

steps.name: Maintainer builds the static viewer page that renders those links in the browser
steps.notes: The viewer is the change template with the data removed and a CSP forbidding all requests.

observations: Changed-symbol detection is done three times with near-identical loops: flowmap/lens.py:analyse, flowmap/change.py:facts and flowmap/atlas.py:overlay each call changed_lines/symbols_at/defs and classify new vs modified separately, so lens, change and atlas --pr can disagree on what 'changed' means.

flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes reads generated Markdown (QUESTIONS.md) back with a regex to recover data that reconcile.py:main already had in memory; an edit to reconcile.py:write_questions_md silently breaks atlas.
flowmap/canvas.py:from_page scrapes `const DATA = {...};` out of a rendered atlas.html, coupling canvas to the atlas template's exact text.

The `CLI flowmap callgraph` entry point serves four unrelated jobs (summary, dump, check, impact) in one __main__ block (flowmap/callgraph.py:__main__); check is a setup step while impact is a review step, so one inventory endpoint has to appear in two flows.

Module-level side effects at import: flowmap/lens.py reads config and compiles CODE/MAP, flowmap/diagrams.py reads ENGINE_ROOT/PLUMBING/APP_DIRS, flowmap/atlas.py fixes OUT, flowmap/verify.py fixes ROOT. atlas, canvas and change all import these, so config is frozen at first import (config.load/root are also @cache).
flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.system is called by flowmap/atlas.py:data purely for its side effect of filling d.matrix ('d.system()  # fills d.matrix'), a read that writes hidden state.

flowmap/reconcile.py:tested_endpoints has a special CLI heuristic that greps test text for the module's file name or 'import <module>', a much weaker notion of 'tested' than the path match used for HTTP endpoints.

bin/flowmap-pr-hook and bin/flowmap are shell/script entry points a person or Claude Code hook runs but they are not in inventory.json (the cli adapter only scans flowmap/*.py), so the PR hook flow described in README is invisible to the map.
